prompt: Diethyl ether and THF form peroxides on storage in air. Why is this dangerous?

options.label: The α-C-H to O is weakened by O's lone pair; O₂ abstracts it to form explosive α-hydroperoxides
Ethers polymerize into glassy solid plastics that clog glassware and seal reactions shut
Ethers' very low BP causes explosive evaporation if sealed in a warm bottle
Ethers dissolve so much O₂ that the gas evolves violently when heated for distillation

explanation: O lone pair donates into the σ* of the α-C-H, weakening it. Over time, atmospheric O₂ abstracts those H's → α-hydroperoxide (R-O-C(OOH)R'). Peroxides concentrate when distilling and detonate. ALWAYS test old ethers for peroxides (KI starch paper) before use, and never distill to dryness.
